method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-02.
questions: Why does a performance/self-assessment pattern not uniquely establish a metacognitive mechanism or a universal learning curve?

evidence.excerpt: The underlying cause of the Dunning-Kruger effect is widely disputed.
As more samples are collected both “expert” and “novice” data points begin to rank closer to the average.
The Dunning-Kruger effect was first discovered and written about in 1999 by researchers David Dunning and Justin Kruger at Cornell University.

In effect, improving the skills of the participants—on humor, grammar, and logical reasoning—helped them recognize the limitations of their own metacognitive abilities and predict their own scores better on subsequent trials.

sources.annotation: Freely readable secondary map of the original self-assessment proposal and statistical objections; the original papers were not independently read and unsupported stage diagrams are excluded.
